subject.title: fix(sessions): cap in-memory session history to prevent unbounded growth

question: Does inspectable exact-head Gateway SSE evidence confirm the bounded window and cursor behavior, and is bounding retained state sufficient scope for the linked OOM issue despite full-transcript initialization and refresh reads?
rationale: The code and focused tests support the steady-state fix, but the automated proof check does not execute the PR’s real Gateway path and the canonical report describes OOM risk broadly.

options.title: Require Gateway proof
options.body: Keep the PR open until a redacted authenticated SSE artifact demonstrates initialization, append, refresh, the 500-message window, nextCursor, and older-page retrieval on the exact head.

options.title: Accept steady-state scope
options.body: Accept retained-state bounding as the fix and track peak full-transcript read memory separately after exact-head validation.

options.title: Require broader memory fix
options.body: Pause this implementation if the canonical issue must also bound initialization and refresh peak memory in the same change.

recommendation.title: Require Gateway proof
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open until a redacted authenticated SSE artifact demonstrates initialization, append, refresh, the 500-message window, nextCursor, and older-page retrieval on the exact head.
